purpose: Sealed-evaluation baseline comparing a second Google model against the pinned transaction-path model. Run on the same sealed corpus, the same agent instructions, and the same strict validators as the canonical gemini-3.5-flash evaluation, via src/run-eval-baseline.mjs. Raw predictions are intentionally not committed because free-text explanations could echo sealed-corpus content; the run is reproducible with the committed runner.
endpoint: Vertex AI managed chat completions (global), Application Default Credentials, no API key
schema_enforcement: response_format json_schema, exported from the same Zod contracts the canonical pipeline uses
findings: Gemma 4 produced zero safe refusals: on all four sealed cases where refusing is the correct answer, it answered anyway. The transaction-path model must refuse on ambiguity, so this alone disqualifies it from the transaction path.
Without API-level structured-output enforcement Gemma scored 0/72 schema-valid; with response_format json_schema it reached 57/72. Structured-output enforcement is load-bearing for this workflow.
Neither model emitted forbidden content in any attempt.
